jobs.occupation: Principal Software Engineer
jobs.description:
The Siteimprove Search Insights team builds the tools our customers use to understand and improve how their content performs in search, both in classic search engines and in the AI assistants that increasingly answer questions on their behalf. We work at enterprise scale, with large volumes of crawled and third party search data, visibility and ranking analysis, and features that turn that data into recommendations marketers can act on.

We are also changing how we build. AI is part of every step, from requirements, to breaking work down, to implementing and reviewing it with coding agents. We are looking for a Principal Software Engineer who wants to build this way, and who helps us define the standard while we do it.

Tech stack you will be working with

• C# and .NET, TypeScript, React

• AWS, Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes

• Event driven services and large scale data pipelines

• GitHub Actions for CI and CD

• Claude Code and other coding agents, MCP servers, Jira and Confluence as the working surface for the AI PDLC

What we will be doing

• Contribute to the technical direction of the team. Write the system designs for the work you own, take part in design reviews, and argue for the option you believe is right.

• Design and build systems yourself: services, APIs and data pipelines that stay stable, fast and affordable as data volumes grow.

• Lead our use of AI across the product development lifecycle. Take a product requirements document to a technical vision and system designs, break it into epics and user stories that an agent can act on, and set the standard at each step.

• Improve the scaffolding that makes agent driven delivery work: context and instruction files, prompts and skills, and the review and testing practice that keeps quality high when code arrives faster than before.

• Keep search data trustworthy, with tests, monitoring and errors a colleague can understand.

• Define how we measure quality, detect drift, and explain results to customers who make decisions based on them.

• Mentor engineers at all levels through design reviews, pairing and written technical proposals, including how to work well with agents.

• Treat cost, performance and operability as design inputs from the start.

• Take part in the daily work of the team: refinement, estimation, prototyping, debugging and production support.

• Travel may be required; a valid passport is required

• Perform other duties as assigned

What we will require of you

• Bachelor's or master's degree in computer science.

• 10 or more years of professional software development experience.

• 5 or more years building and running services and APIs on a public cloud, preferably AWS.

• A track record of architecture decisions that span several teams, including the trade offs you rejected and why.

• You have owned features or services end to end, including what happened after they were released.

• Hands on experience using coding agents in real production work, with a clear view of where they help and where they do not.

• Deep understanding of software design principles, algorithms and data structures, and a commitment to technical excellence.

• Excellent written and verbal English. You write proposals and designs that other people, and agents, can act on without a meeting.

• Willingness to work across the stack when the problem calls for it.

What we will love about you

• Experience turning product requirements into technical designs and a delivery plan that a team can execute.

• Experience with search, SEO, crawling, indexing, ranking or web scale data.

• Experience with infrastructure as code such as Terraform or CloudFormation.

• Experience working in a team distributed across Europe and North America.

• You take pride in the work of the team and lead by example.

• You are comfortable replacing what you built yesterday with something better today.

What you'll love about usWe’re building the next generation of AI-powered content intelligence, helping organizations unify accessibility, SEO/AEO, analytics, and content performance into one platform. If you’re energized by solving complex problems, working cross-functionally, and contributing to a product with real-world impact, we’d love to connect.

In addition, we hope you will appreciate:

At Siteimprove, we're committed to supporting your wellbeing both at work and beyond. Our Denmark benefits are designed to help you thrive personally and professionally.

Rest and relaxation: Generous time off including Danish holiday entitlements, five additional FF Days, child sick leave, and bereavement leave.

Comprehensive benefits: Health insurance, company-paid mobile phone support, and internet allowance to support your day-to-day needs.

Prepare for the future: Danica pension with employer contributions to help support your retirement goals.

jobs.occupation: Project coordinator position, Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Aarhus University
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a two-year, fixed-term position as Project Coordinator in Professor Daan van Aalten’s research group at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Aarhus University.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two-year position, starting on 15 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The working hours are 30 hours per week.

Job description
As Project Coordinator, you will support Professor Daan van Aalten’s research group and its externally funded projects at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Aarhus University.

Your main tasks will be to:

• Coordinate the administration of an international research project with the University of Aberdeen and the Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine (TIGEM) in Pozzuoli, Italy. This includes arranging partner meetings and following up on agreed actions and deadlines.
• Assist researchers with organizing and structuring research data, including patient data received from collaborators at TIGEM.
• Support grant applications and prepare and update project budgets, including staff costs, employment periods and overheads.
• Keep project documentation up to date and work with AU finance and research support staff on budget changes and reporting requirements.
• Support recruitment and contract extensions in cooperation with HR, and coordinate practical arrangements when researchers, students and visiting staff join or leave the group, including AU access, introductions and handovers.
• Organize group meetings, workshops and retreats, and arrange visits by collaborators and prospective group members.
• Prepare and update internal guides and onboarding materials, including information about group contacts, equipment responsibilities and practical laboratory routines.
• Prepare staff surveys and follow up on feedback about communication, working routines and the working environment.
You will also help group members with AU administrative systems and procedures, put them in contact with the relevant university services and handle other administrative tasks as needed.

Your profile
Applicants must hold a master’s degree or equivalent qualification. A PhD is an advantage, particularly in relation to working in an academic research environment.

We are looking for a proactive, well-organized colleague with good communication skills. You should be able to work independently, prioritize your tasks and keep track of deadlines.

Experience with research administration, grant applications and project budgets, including staff costs and overheads, is an advantage. Knowledge of university HR and finance procedures and experience with recruitment support and onboarding would also be useful.

You should be fluent in written and spoken Danish and English and enjoy working with researchers, students and administrative staff. Knowledge of Italian is an advantage when working with colleagues at TIGEM.

Who we are
The Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics is part of the Faculty of Natural Sciences, Aarhus University and comprises research within the areas of Plant Molecular Biology, Neurobiology, RNA Biology and Innovation, Protein Science,

Cellular Health, Intervention and Nutrition. There are currently 75 full-time scientific staff and 95 PhD students. The department is responsible for two educations: Molecular Biology and Molecular Medicine with a yearly uptake of 160 students in total.

Please refer to http://mbg.au.dk/ for further information about The Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics and to https://nat.au.dk/ and http://www.au.dk/ for information on Faculty of Natural Sciences and Aarhus University, respectively.

What we offer
We offer a varied administrative role in an international research environment, with close collaboration with researchers, students and university administrative staff. The position provides opportunities to develop experience in research administration, grant support and project coordination, and to contribute to the organization and working environment of the research group.

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is at Universitetsbyen 81, 8000 Aarhus C, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with affiliated institutions.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Professor Daan van Aalten, +45 93 58 82 72, daan@au.dk

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 26 November 2026.

Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an Administrator (fuldmægtig) with an availability allowance on basic salary grades 4–8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

jobs.occupation: 4 PhD positions in AI-accelerated development of PFAS-free polymer-based battery materials cells in Self-driving Laboratories - DTU Energy and BRIGHT
jobs.description:
Are you interested in a career in AI for materials and in accelerating the green transition? If so, we have a number of positions at DTU that might just right for you. 

The four PhD positions at DTU Energy are part of BRIGHT's mission-oriented Novel Biomanufacturing-Enabled Materials research programme, referred to as Mission 1A, which aims to create new classes of PFAS-free functional biomaterials through biotechnology. The mission's current focus are proteinaceous materials with defined composition, programmable chemistry and controlled assembly as sustainable alternatives to persistent fluorinated materials. The scientific scope spans AI-guided protein and peptide design, microbial engineering, non-canonical amino acid biosynthesis and incorporation, cell-free prototyping, fermentation, purification, materials processing, analytical quality control and structure-function characterization. The programme focuses on building an integrated pipeline from molecular design to scalable biomanufacturing and material testing, with explicit attention to manufacturability, cost, sustainability and industrial translation. Batteries provide the first proof-of-concept application, because PFAS-containing materials are currently used in several battery components and because this sector imposes strict requirements for stability, processability and performance. The broader ambition is to establish a versatile biomanufacturing platform for advanced PFAS-free materials with future relevance across energy technologies, coatings, electronics and other high-value applications.

You will work closely with experimental and computational colleagues in BRIGHT and in DTU Energy, as well as with our international collaborators, e.g., on the use cases on advanced battery materials in MaterialsCommons for Europe and on the development of Self-driving Laboratories (SDLs) at the Pioneer Center CAPeX. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
All four positions are centered on the application of novel PFAS-free proteins and polypeptides for applications in sustainable batteries. The design space for finding optimal compositions and synthesis conditions for such polymers for use as, e.g., electrolytes, binders and additives is vast, we are combining self-driving labs, high-throughput machine learning simulations, and agentic AI to transition to digitalization-based autonomous development of high-performing PFAS-free polymer materials for high-performant batteries, i.e., high electrochemical stability, ionic conductivity, coulombic efficiency, and cyclability at a low cost. The positions will target for areas specifically

• Development of automated setup for high-throughput testing of solid polymer electrolytes and binders, e.g., chemical and electrochemical stability, preparation and film casting. 
• Development of automated setup for in situ polymerization of sodium/sodium-based based battery materials
• Self-driving lab modules for autonomous testing of mechanical properties of polymer-based battery materials, interfaces and layers
• Self-driving lab modules for assembly and testing of advanced (e.g., solid-state and anode-less, sodium-based button and coin cell batteries.
Qualifications:

• Good working knowledge of electrochemistry.
• Ability to work independently and plan and carry out complicated tasks.
• Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken.
• A proactive approach to problem-solving, capable of identifying new directions and opportunities within the project.
Desirable Qualifications:

• Experience with self-driving laboratories or building custom experimental hardware
• Experience in polymer or battery chemistry 
• Experience in machine learning or computational chemistry/materials science
• Experience in Python programming and version control/git
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

The positions are full-time positions. The preferred starting date is 1 February 2027 (or according to mutual agreement).

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Professor, Director Tejs Vegge: teve@dtu.dk and Professor Johan Hjelm: johh@dtu.dk 

You can read more about DTU Energy at www.energy.dtu.dk./

Find more information about BRIGHT: https://bright.dtu.dk/, MaterialsCommons: https://www.materialscommons.eu and The Pioneer Center CAPeX: https://www.capex.dtu.dk

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 15 December 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae

• Up to two letters of recommendation
Please indicate which of the positions you would potentially be interested in (you can select all).

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

About BRIGHT – The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRIGHT) is a major initiative based at DTU that aims to accelerate the development of biosolutions and strengthen the bio-based economy. BRIGHT serves as a hub for academic and industrial partners working together to unlock the potential of bioproduction. BRIGHT focuses on three main areas: Sustainable materials (Developing bio-based alternatives to fossil-derived materials), Microbial foods (Innovating food production through microbial technologies), and Microorganisms for net-zero agriculture (Creating solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in agriculture). The goal is to develop and scale innovative biosolutions within these areas, ultimately creating sustainable and competitive alternatives to fossil-based products and processes that can make significant contributions to reducing global greenhouse gas emissions.

The Department of Energy Conversion and Storage (DTU Energy) focuses on research and development of functional materials, components, and systems for sustainable energy technologies. The technologies include fuel cells, electrolysis, power-to-x, batteries, and carbon capture. The research is based on strong competences on electrochemistry, atomic scale and multi-physics modelling, autonomous materials discovery, materials processing, and structural analyses. We also focus on educating engineering students at all levels, ranging from BSc, MSc, PhD to lifelong learning students. We have about 300 dedicated employees. Read more about us at www.energy.dtu.dk.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Experimental Quantum Nanophotonics
jobs.description:
PhD Project in quantum and nonlinear light–matter interactions in plasmonic nanocavities

  The Niels Bohr Institute
 Faculty of SCIENCE

  University of Copenhagen

  The Niels Bohr Institute invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in experimental quantum nanophotonics. The project will be part of the newly established Mikkelsen Photonics group (Quantum, nonlinear and nanoscale light–matter interactions), funded by a Novo Nordisk Foundation RECRUIT grant.

  Start date is (expected to be) 15 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project

  Plasmonic nanocavities confine light to volumes thousands of times below the diffraction limit. In such extreme gaps, emission rates are enhanced by orders of magnitude, strong field gradients appear, and the usual rules of light–matter interaction are rewritten. The project builds on a wafer-scale platform developed in the group, in which colloidal quantum emitters (quantum dots or nanoplatelets) are deterministically placed into thousands of lithographically defined nanocavities with a controlled number of emitters per cavity. The PhD student will develop this platform and use it to study one or more of the following:

   	
• Few-emitter quantum optics: single-photon emission, collective emission, energy transfer and strong coupling with one to a few emitters per cavity. 	
• Cavity-enhanced nonlinear optics: using the extreme field confinement and field gradients of the nanogap to enhance and control nonlinear processes. 	
• Active and electrically tunable nanocavities: integrating functional materials (e.g. ferroelectric or two-dimensional materials) into the gap to switch and tune the emitter–cavity interaction.   The work is primarily experimental and involves nanofabrication, optical spectroscopy (photoluminescence, single-photon and photon-correlation measurements, nonlinear spectroscopy), optoelectronic device characterization and electromagnetic simulations. The specific project will be defined together with the successful candidate.

  Who are we looking for?

  We are looking for candidates within the fields of electrical engineering, physics, nanoscience, photonics, materials science or related areas. Applicants can have a background from optoelectronic or nanophotonic devices, semiconductor nanomaterials, optical spectroscopy, nanofabrication or electromagnetic simulation, but we will also consider candidates with different backgrounds. Hands-on experience with optical experiments and an interest in building new experimental setups is an advantage.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?

  The Mikkelsen Photonics group was established at the Niels Bohr Institute in 2026, when Prof. Maiken H. Mikkelsen moved from Duke University (USA) supported by a Novo Nordisk Foundation RECRUIT grant. The group studies quantum, nonlinear and nanoscale light–matter interactions in plasmonic nanocavities and is building a new laboratory combining deeply subwavelength cavities, single-photon spectroscopy, femtosecond pump–probe spectroscopy and, in a later phase, cryogenic and high-magnetic-field operation. As one of the first members of the group, the PhD student will have a central role in shaping the experiments and the scientific direction, with close supervision. The group is part of the Quantum Optics and Photonics research area at the Niels Bohr Institute, home to the Center for Hybrid Quantum Networks (Hy-Q), and has access to the nanofabrication facilities at the Niels Bohr Institute and the DTU Nanolab cleanroom.

  The group is a part of the Niels Bohr Institute, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen, in the new laboratory and office building of the Niels Bohr Institute.

  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and new, dedicated optics and nanofabrication facilities.

  Principal supervisor is Prof. Maiken H. Mikkelsen, The Niels Bohr Institute, maiken.mikkelsen@nbi.ku.dk.

  The PhD programme

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree.

  ************************************************************************

  Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Electrical Engineering, Physics, Nanoscience, Photonics or Materials Science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor’s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Physics.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year.

  A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.

  When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in experimental nanophotonics and quantum optics 	
• Good language skills   ************************************************************************

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include

   	
• Motivated letter of application, including your motivation for applying for this specific PhD project (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Application deadline:

  The deadline for applications is 26 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held shortly after the application deadline.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor, Prof. Maiken H. Mikkelsen, maiken.mikkelsen@nbi.ku.dk.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in AI-driven knowledge graphs and network models of plant stress responses
jobs.description:
The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in computational plant biology. The project is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation through the Ascending Investigator grant “Accelerating crop resilience with AI-enabled gene function prediction and stress regulatory networks” (NNF26OC0113093). The programme aims to make heat and drought resilience engineering in Nordic crops predictable by converting the plant literature and multi-omics data into evidence-backed predictions of gene function and stress regulation.

  Start date is expected to be 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project  Most plant genes remain functionally uncharacterised, and the knowledge that does exist is scattered across more than 200,000 articles. Our knowledge graph PlantConnectome has shown that large language models can extract this knowledge at scale; this project will build its successor and use it to predict gene function.

  You will:

   	
• Fine-tune open large language models (e.g. Llama-class models with QLoRA) on our existing, curated knowledge graph, and use the best checkpoint to extract entities, relationships and supporting evidence from >200,000 open-access plant articles spanning model species and crops 	
• Build a provenance-aware knowledge graph an order of magnitude larger than PlantConnectome, in which every edge is traceable to the sentence and experiment that supports it 	
• Predict new gene–GO associations by direct-neighbourhood reasoning (matching LLM-generated entity definitions to GO terms with embeddings and an LLM guardrail) and by path-based link prediction with graph neural networks, evaluated CAFA-style against held-out annotations 	
• Turn regulatory relationships in the graph into Boolean and related discrete network models of stress signalling, simulate them, and test their predictions against expression data generated in the group 	
• Distinguish well-supported from over-cited claims, and represent evidence quality and independence explicitly in the graph   The position is computational, but sits in a group that generates its own single-cell stress data and validates predictions in rapeseed, so your predictions will be tested.

  Who are we looking for?  We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, physics, mathematics or plant biology with a strong quantitative interest. Experience with natural language processing, large language models, graph databases, network modelling or machine learning is an advantage. An interest in how plants actually work is essential; a formal background in plant biology is not.

  What we value  Coding experience is welcome but not required at entry – we teach it. What we cannot teach quickly, and therefore select for, is scientific judgment:

   	
• questioning data rather than accepting it – asking what was measured, how, and against which expectation 	
• noticing anomalies and treating them as information rather than noise 	
• organising several lines of investigation in parallel and knowing when to stop or redirect one 	
• connecting computational evidence to a concrete biological question 	
• changing your mind when the evidence changes   We are equally interested in candidates from biology who want to learn computation and candidates from computer science, physics or engineering who want to learn biology.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?  The Mutwil group at PLEN works at the interface of comparative and evolutionary plant biology and AI-driven biological discovery. We build large cross-species gene expression atlases, comparative co-expression networks and knowledge graphs, and we use machine learning and large language models to turn the plant literature and omics archives into testable hypotheses. The group comprises several PhD students, postdocs and master’s students, and maintains a portfolio of widely used community resources under the .plant.tools domain, including PlantConnectome, CoNekt, diurnal.plant.tools and evorepro.plant.tools.

  Employment as a PhD fellow is full time and for a maximum of 3 years. Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals

  Please include:

This PhD project is part of a BRIGHT programme developing a general platform for the design of protein- and peptide-based biomaterials, with solid-state battery components as its first testbed. Our goal is to replace fluorinated PFAS polymers with de novo designed proteins and peptides.

You will generate the computational designs at the heart of the platform, by combining molecular foundation models with iterative laboratory feedback. You will develop design algorithms for biomaterials with natural and non-natural amino acids, and for planning their biosynthesis and biomanufacturing. You will develop lab-in-the-loop algorithms that use generative model-controlled stochastic synthesis to maximize information gain at every round of experimental testing.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Responsibilities:

• Generate de novo peptide and protein designs meeting multiple coupled property targets, including adhesion, cohesion, ion conduction and controlled degradability
• Use and adapt generative molecular design tools such as RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and AlphaFold-type models
• Develop and extend information-dense synthesis algorithms to manufacture designs in the laboratory 
• Extend these methods to expanded genetic codes, so that non-canonical residues can be encoded and biosynthesised rather than only chemically synthesised
• Develop methods to learn from diverse measurements of material properties, via shared latent representations 
• Develop methods to continuously learn from iterative experimentation, by feeding back experimental data into an integrated model with quantified uncertainty
• Work closely with experimentalists to optimize experimental designs for collecting high-information training data
• Work closely with experimentalists to automate and scale up design-build-test-learn cycles
• Report your research results in peer-reviewed scientific publications and international conferences
• Collaborate within the research group and our local, national and international networks
• Disseminate your results through public engagement and social media
• Teach and supervise MSc and BSc students as well as research assistants
Qualifications:

• MSc in computational biology, bioinformatics, biophysics, computer science or a related area
• Programming experience in Python
• Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch
• Excellent English proficiency in written and oral form
• Excellent communication and social skills for working within an interdisciplinary research team
• Strong analytical skills and ability to work independently
Preferred qualifications but not mandatory:

• Knowledge of protein structure and molecular biology
• Experience with protein design tools such as RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN or AlphaFold
• Familiarity with DNA-encoded libraries, genetic code expansion or next-generation sequencing
• Interest in multi-objective optimisation, reinforcement learning, and bridging computational design with experimental realisation
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Animal and Veterinary Sciences programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
Maximizing use of fresh grass for dairy cows by combining grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards

Research area and project description:
We are seeking a dedicated PhD student for a 3-year position within the topic of dairy production with fresh grass as a main forage source.

The impact of dairy production on environment and climate is of continued importance and interest. Cropping and feeding fresh grass can potentially improve the impact of dairy production on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen leakage to surrounding fresh waters.

The project investigates the potential of maximizing fresh grass forage intake to reduce enteric methane emission and increase nitrogen utilization, while maintaining milk production. A series of trials with lactating dairy cows are planned investigating combinations of grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards.

This project offers:
 
• A unique opportunity to contribute to a more sustainable agriculture and environmental-friendly milk production
• An active and stimulating academic environment with several other PhD students and early career staff
• Access to state-of-the-art research facilities for both barn-housing, grazing, and pasture management for dairy cattle
• Collaboration with a range of research partners
• Collaborative projects that foster innovative thinking and practical implementation
Qualifications and specific competences:
Applicants to the PhD position must hold a relevant university degree (MSc) in Animal Science, Agricultural Science, or related fields.

The candidate is expected to have:
 
• Understanding of ruminant nutrition and digestion
• Experience with data handling and analysis using at least one software.
• Ability and interest in collaborating across disciplines with project partners.
• Ability to communicate effectively in English.
• Good scientific and writing skills.
